source.title: Phases of learning dynamics in artificial neural networks in the absence or presence of mislabeled data

page_placements.theme: Ordinary late-training overfitting and its dependence on noise or capacity

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study measures test error over training time, but does not reproduce the original double-descent method or sweep model size.
record.gate_note: The study reports test-error dynamics over epochs with randomly mislabeled data. It does not sweep model size or training-sample count, and its discussion of double descent cites prior work and proposes studying its mechanism in future work. The cleaning results report test accuracy, not test error, and are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: The study did not set out to test double descent. It does report full test-error trajectories over up to about 1000 epochs for a label-noise MNIST network trained to interpolation. That is the setting where V2 predicts a second descent, so its results bear on V2 in a new, small-network setting.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. With mislabeled data, SGD passes through four phases: test error falls, stays low, rises while mislabeled samples are learned, then plateaus high. Order parameters on gradient alignment explain the phase transitions. Phase II enables cleaning of mislabeled samples. Double descent is mentioned only in the summary, as prior work and as a mechanism for future study.
record.recipe_differences: Measures SGD learning dynamics over epochs with mislabeled data; does not sweep model size or reproduce a double-descent experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: The minimum and final test errors vary with the fraction of mislabeled samples; the minimum rises sharply beyond a threshold and approaches the final error when the mislabeled fraction is greater than 0.85.

fits_no_version.finding: Final test error rises roughly linearly with mislabeled fraction ρ. Minimum test error is flat at small ρ, then rises sharply toward final error above ρ≈0.85.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In small label-noise networks, the size of the late-training test-error rise scales with the fraction of mislabeled samples.

fits_no_version.finding: The time of minimum test error tm is nearly independent of ρ, while the time to fit all training data tf grows with ρ (Fig 3C).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The onset of epoch-wise overfitting to label noise is delayed as the mislabeled fraction grows, while the best-test-error epoch is unchanged.

record.problems: For the claim-relevant results, test-error curves are primarily presented in figures and exact values are not stated. The paper gives only a brief statement of similar CIFAR10 results without detailed curves or values. It does not test model-size or sample-count double descent.

untested.parts: Large or wide models, where the originals say epoch-wise double descent appears. Dependence on model size. A clean-label epoch-wise test-error curve. Explicit CIFAR10 curves.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
No effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Noise fraction is varied, but no peak, multiple descent or optimal regularization is examined.

missing.what: Timescales tm (test-error minimum) and tf (training-loss minimum) as functions of ρ. These locate the rise along the epoch axis, relevant when comparing epoch-wise curve timing.

record.verdict_notes: Labelled limits_scope rather than challenges for two reasons: the network is small, and Nakkiran et al. state epoch-wise double descent needs sufficiently large models. A researcher may judge the plateau a challenge to an unqualified V2. Exact curve values are only in figures, and the ρ used in Fig 3(A) is unstated.

versions.untested_parts: No model-size sweep or interpolation-threshold analysis.
The reported epoch-wise curves concern training with mislabeled data; the study does not report a corresponding clean-label epoch-wise test-error curve.
The study varies the fraction of mislabeled samples, not the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
No comparison of capacity sweeps across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is tested as a predictor of peak location across size, epochs, or sample count.
The paper varies label-noise fraction but does not test whether a double-descent peak is driven by noise, splits into multiple peaks, or disappears under optimally tuned regularization.
No re-counting of complexity by effective parameter number.

rows.operation_detail: Measured test error over training epochs with randomly mislabeled training samples.
rows.value: The text reports that test error decreases during phase I (0–10 epoch), stays roughly the same during phase II (10–70 epoch), increases during phase III (70–200 epoch), and reaches a high plateau during phase IV.
rows.note: The reported trajectory has a fall, a rise, and then a high plateau, rather than a second fall. Exact plotted test-error values are not stated.
rows.check: State should be absent, not reversed. Test error falls, then rises to a high plateau with no second descent. That is classical overfitting, not the opposite of double descent. Mislabeled fraction for Fig 3(A) is not stated, as recorded.

relationships.condition: Small fully connected net (2×50 hidden units) on a 4000-sample MNIST subset with random label noise, SGD B=25, α=0.01, trained to about 1000 epochs
relationships.reason: Test error falls, rises once the net fits mislabeled samples, then stays on a high plateau with no second descent (r1, r2). This holds across noise levels. It matches the originals' caveat that small models give only a U-shaped curve.
relationships.display_finding: Across noise levels, test error fell, rose as mislabeled samples were fitted, and remained on a high plateau without a second descent.

source_check.notes: Absence of recovery applies to the reported training trajectories. The study does not sweep network capacity or establish that small capacity causes the missing second descent.

statements.correction: Figure 3: MNIST subset; 400 samples per digit; fully connected network; two hidden layers with 50 units each; SGD B=25, α=0.01. Test error decreases during epochs 0–10, stays roughly constant during epochs 10–70, increases during epochs 70–200, and reaches a high plateau afterward. Similar four-phase trajectories occur across a wide range of label-noise fractions.
statements.problem: The cited rows do not report any of the listed architectures, width comparisons, or training conditions. This study does not establish that capacity changes the trajectory's shape.
